text:
Seth Meyers has mocked Donald Trump on his show(Image: Late Night with Seth Meyers)

Seth Meyers has once again mocked Donald Trump on his show while predicting a "spinoff" to the Iran deal.

Even though the president has said several times that he is close to finalizing a deal with Iran, nothing has come to fruition yet. On Thursday, he threatened further attacks on the country in the Middle East - but just hours later, he said he had called off military action, claiming there had been a breakthrough in negotiations.

During a press conference in the Oval Office of the White House on Thursday, Trump declared, "We just made a great settlement of the war with Iran." He offered scant details, other than to say he expects an agreement to extend a fragile ceasefire that started in April to be finalized "over the next few days."

But despite Trump's claims, a spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry said in a live phone call on state television that negotiations were active and nothing had been finalized to end the conflict that began on February 28 when the US and Israel jointly attacked Iran. Addressing Trump's repeated claims that he is close to a deal, Meyers made fun of the president while opening his latest A Closer Look segment last night.

President Donald Trump claimed he has reached a deal with Iran(Image: AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

The TV host and comedian compared the president's lies about the war in Iran to HBO's repeated streaming rebrands - and said that it's "no surprise that even conservative news outlets are losing patience."

Meyers joked, "Trump has promised a deal with Iran more times than HBO has rebranded."

He then said the deal might reach the point where a spinoff - jokingly called The Pitt of Hormuz, a play on the words Strait of Hormuz - might be made.

Meyers told the audience, "At this point, we’ve been through Iran Deal, Iran Deal Go, Iran Deal Now, Iran Deal Plus, Iran Deal Max to just Max, back to Iran Deal Max, back to Iran Deal Plus. I just hope we get a spin off called The Pitt of Hormuz."

The president said a deal will be finalized soon(Image: Late Night with Seth Meyers)

Extending the terms of the ceasefire gives US leaders more time to negotiate over Iran's nuclear program, the main reason Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu used to justify launching the war. Netanyahu's office said on Thursday that Israel is not a party to the emerging agreement between the US and Iran.

The announcement came after two days of back-and-forth attacks between the US and Iran had pushed the Middle East closer to the resumption of a full-scale war. Trump had threatened further escalation earlier on Thursday, posting on social media that the US would hit Iran "VERY HARD TONIGHT" and take "total control" of its oil and gas industries.

He predicted a spinoff to the Iran deal(Image: Late Night with Seth Meyers)

A few hours later, Trump posted on social media that significant points in the negotiations "have been brought to the highest level of Iranian leadership and approved."

Esmail Baghaei, the spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry, said in his phone call on state television that the text of a deal is "mostly finalized."

But the spokesperson added, "The problem is that the contradictions in America’s position have caused turbulence to this process."
